description: Deere (commonly known as John Deere) is an agricultural giant that manufactures and sells tractors, harvesters, loaders, and other equipment used by farmers worldwide. Founded in 1837 as a maker of steel plows pulled by horses, the company has expanded into heavy machinery used for golf course maintenance, snow removal, and logging. The company introduced a self-driving tractor in 2022 and is pushing into machine learning to help increase agricultural production. As of 2024, it was among a small number of companies that have been on the Fortune 500 every year since the list’s inception in 1955.

title: Deere

rankings.title: Change the World
rankings.itemDescription: The agricultural machinery giant is using software, connectivity, and automation to boost farm productivity; cut down on fuel, chemical, and water use; and allow customers to meet input-efficiency and emissions goals. It upgraded its harvest automation system in 2025 to add predictive inputs, which enable farmers to measure crop variability and control ground speed. Autonomous tractors allow farmers to cover more ground during crop cycles, the company says. Meanwhile, Deere has introduced technologies like See & Spray Ultimate, which deploys cameras and machine learning to target weeds.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: Based in Moline, Ill., this maker of tractors, combines, and other agricultural gear endured a tough 2024, as weather disruptions and trade tensions fueled a global downturn in farming. The slump in U.S. homebuilding, meanwhile, hurt its construction equipment division. Overall, Deere’s revenue dropped 16% year over year, to $51.7 billion.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription:
John Deere—the machinery and equipment company famous for its iconic green tractor—had one of its most profitable years ever in 2022, reaching $7 billion, up 20% from the previous year, as it took a page from the tech industry’s playbook, developing self-driving tractors, satellite-linked smart equipment, and a software-as-a-service business.

  • Revenues in 2022 grew 19% as the company was able to pass much of the increase in production costs on to farmers who were flush with cash after corn and soybean prices hit record highs.

  • In May 2023 Deere announced a plan to connect remote farms in Brazil and the U.S. to state-of-the-art machinery via satellite.

  • The tractor maker suffered a legislative setback in Colorado in April 2023 when Gov. Jared Polis signed a “right to repair” bill, enabling farmers to fix their own equipment, thus ending Deere’s monopoly on repairs of its machinery.

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: A staple of American manufacturing for nearly 200 years, Illinois-based Deere makes agricultural and construction machinery as well as diesel engines and lawn care equipment. In 2021, the company posted 24% year-over-year revenue growth. Profits jumped, too, with demand for its machinery snapping back as the global economy rebounded. Deere also smoothed its labor outlook for the near future by reaching a six-year labor agreement with the United Auto Workers union in November 2021, ending a five-week strike. After Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, Deere suspended shipments of machinery to Russia and Belarus.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: Even during a pandemic, people still have to eat. Agriculture was one business to ride out 2020 in a strong position. Deere, the 184-year-old American icon and maker of heavy machinery, saw strong agricultural sales corresponding with the seasonality of farming. That was largely enough to counter the lower demand for construction equipment made by Deere over the same time frame, with construction projects halted owing to COVID-19. Deere, however, still saw revenue fall 9.5%, to $35.5 billion, between 2019 and 2020.

rankings.title: Fortune Global 500
rankings.itemDescription: John May is not even a full year into his tenure as only the 10th chief executive ever to lead the 183-year-old American icon. He finds himself at the helm of the $39.2 billion agricultural giant as it rolls with virus-related punches; Deere briefly suspended production of construction and forestry equipment at some facilities amid weakened demand and pivoted to manufacturing 400,000 face shields for health care workers. For 2019, the company's revenue rose 5.1% year-over-year and profits spiked by 37%, to $3.3 billion. But even before the pandemic, Deere said it expected sales to fall at least 10% in 2020.

rankings.itemDescription: John May is seven months into his tenure as only the 10th chief executive ever to lead the 183-year-old American icon. He finds himself at the helm of the $39.2 billion agricultural giant as it rolls with virus-related punches; Deere briefly suspended production of construction and forestry equipment at some facilities amid weakened demand, and is now manufacturing 400,000 face shields for health care workers. The company's revenue rose 5.1% year-over-year and profits spiked by 37%, to $3.3 billion in 2019. But even before the pandemic, Deere said it expected sales to fall at least 10% in 2020.
